nodes.summary: There exists a finite group $G$ that is not soluble, is totally $2$-closed, and has a nontrivial nilpotent normal subgroup (equivalently, a nontrivial Fitting subgroup).
nodes.title: A finite insoluble totally 2-closed group with nontrivial Fitting subgroup

nodes.summary: The statement, asked by M. Arezoomand, M. A. Iranmanesh, C. E. Praeger and G. Tracey, that there exists a finite group $G$ that is not soluble, is totally $2$-closed, and has a nontrivial nilpotent normal subgroup (equivalently, a nontrivial Fitting subgroup).
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 20.1 (insoluble totally 2-closed groups)

nodes.summary: A group $G$ is totally $2$-closed when every faithful action of $G$ on a set $\Omega$ is $2$-closed; equivalently, in each faithful permutation representation of $G$ on a set $\Omega$, $G$ is the largest subgroup of $\mathrm{Sym}(\Omega)$ preserving each of its orbits on $\Omega^2$.
nodes.title: Totally 2-closed groups

nodes.summary: An action of a group $G$ on a set $\Omega$ is $2$-closed when every permutation $\sigma$ of $\Omega$ that preserves each $G$-orbit on ordered pairs (that is, for all $\alpha, \beta \in \Omega$ some $g \in G$ satisfies $\sigma(\alpha) = g \alpha$ and $\sigma(\beta) = g \beta$) is induced by an element of $G$: there is $g \in G$ with $\sigma(\omega) = g \omega$ for all $\omega \in \Omega$.
nodes.title: 2-closed actions

nodes.summary: There exist a finite set $\Omega$, a solvable subgroup $G$ of the symmetric group $\mathrm{Sym}(\Omega)$, and a composition factor $S$ of the $2$-closure $G^{(2)}$ of $G$ such that $S$ is not cyclic and $S$ is not isomorphic to the alternating group $A_n$ for any $n$. nodes.title: Skresanov's counterexample to Kourovka Problem 19.67

nodes.summary: The statement that for every finite set $\Omega$ and every solvable subgroup $G$ of the symmetric group $\mathrm{Sym}(\Omega)$, every composition factor of the $2$-closure $G^{(2)}$ of $G$ is cyclic or isomorphic to the alternating group $A_n$ for some natural number $n$.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 19.67

nodes.summary: For a subgroup $G$ of the symmetric group $\mathrm{Sym}(\Omega)$, the $2$-closure $G^{(2)}$ of $G$ is the subgroup of $\mathrm{Sym}(\Omega)$ generated by the permutations $\sigma$ that map every pair of points into its $G$-orbit, that is, such that for all $\alpha, \beta \in \Omega$ there is $g \in G$ with $g(\alpha) = \sigma(\alpha)$ and $g(\beta) = \sigma(\beta)$.
nodes.title: The $2$-closure of a permutation group
